findings.how: Round 1 (746795b): registry.ts shortHostName. A host also answers to the first part of its id, its host part and its resolved hostname. That part must have a letter plus a digit or a hyphen, be at least MIN_NAME long, and the name must not be an address. A short name two hosts share goes to both, so it gets TWO_NAMED. offer_connect uses the registry's names. Round 2 fixes the verifier's must-fix on the longest-run rule (2f19d80). In resolve.ts, runsNaming now lets a longer run hide a shorter one only when writtenOnto() holds. That means each of the longer run's extra words is joined to the next one by exactly one '-', '_' or '.', or by spaces when the extra word is a number. The gap is read from folded.slice(ws[k-1].end, ws[k].start). Otherwise both runs stay, so TWO_NAMED asks as it did at 1b39bb3. With db-01 and db-01-backup, 'on db-01, backup…', 'on db-01: …', 'on db-01. Backup…', 'on db-01 backup…' and 'on build-01, test the backup' now give TWO_NAMED. 'on db-01-backup, …', 'on db-01_backup', 'build-01.other.net' and 'in Ubuntu 24.04' / 'Ubuntu 24 04' still pick the longer name. 'on build-01. Other net jobs…' does not read build-01.other.net. bindTarget's check of the model's choice uses the same rule. Docs §1 'Short names' and resolve.ts's header now describe the rule. I re-ran the verifier's db.ts probe on the branch: all three comma, colon and full-stop forms now give TWO_NAMED, and db-01-backup still binds.

verifierProblems.what: Regression from 746795b (#180). shortDistroName gives a distro its first word whatever that word is: build-env becomes "build", test-box "test", work-vm "work", home-lab "home", dev-ubuntu "dev" and the-box "the". Names like these are common for distros made with wsl --import. I ran bindTarget over buildRegistry's names (win32, WSL on, distros Ubuntu-22.04, build-env, test-box, work-vm). "delete the logs in build" binds to wsl:build-env, "save it in test mode" to wsl:test-box and "clean up old files in work" to wsl:work-vm. At 1b39bb3 all three bind to local, because no whole distro name was said. With build-env bound, otherTargetsNamed has nothing to count, so D4.4's wrong-target guard does not make the delete ask. A destructive request about a local folder can now be announced and run inside a WSL distro. Hosts got a safety rule (shortHostName needs a letter plus a digit or a hyphen, so 'in the app' names nothing), but distros got none. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix-verify/remote/scr/names.ts.

Otherwise return null. A looser alternative is to accept it when everything after it is a version. Add tests to targets-registry and targets-runtime: with a build-env distro, 'delete the logs in build' still binds to local, and 'in Ubuntu' still binds to Ubuntu-22.04.

The same happens with build-01 and build-01-test for 'on build-01, test the backup', and for the voice form without a comma. otherTargetsNamed still counts db-01, so a dangerous command asks, but anything else runs on the wrong computer without a question.
